record.original_question: In quantitative logic, a formula is assigned a meta-degree by aggregating its truth degrees over all evaluations of its propositional variables, using either a normalized weighted sum on a finite truth-degree set or an integral on [0,1]. Which other kinds of aggregation operators are suitable for defining these meta-degrees, and how should the choice of aggregation operator depend on the intended applications of the logic?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1 (S. Gottwald). Which other types of aggregation operators instead of the integral or the weighted sum are suitable here? And how depends their choice from intended applications?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In quantitative logic one assigns to each propositional formula $\varphi(p_1,\dots,p_n)$ a so-called meta-degree, which measures the overall truth-value of $\varphi$ obtained by aggregating its truth degrees over all evaluations of the propositional variables. Two standard choices are used:

(a) If the truth-degree set is a finite chain $L=\{a_0<a_1<\dots<a_m\}\subset[0,1]$ with a probability distribution $(w_0,\dots,w_m)$ on $L$, then the meta-degree of $\varphi$ is defined as the normalized weighted sum
$$	au(\varphi)=\sum_{v\in L^n} \Bigl(\prod_{i=1}^{n} w(v(p_i))\Bigr)\,  ar v(\varphi),$$
where $ ar v(\varphi)\in L$ denotes the truth-value of $\varphi$ under the evaluation $v:\{p_1,\dots,p_n\}	o L$.

(b) If the truth-degree set is the unit interval $[0,1]$ equipped with the Lebesgue (or another) probability measure $\mu$, then the meta-degree of $\varphi$ is defined as the integral
$$	au(\varphi)=\int_{[0,1]^n}  ar v(\varphi)\,d\mu^n(v),$$
where $ ar v:[0,1]^n	o[0,1]$ is the truth-function of $\varphi$ determined by the underlying many-valued logical connectives (e.g. those of \L{}ukasiewicz, Gödel, or product logic).

Determine which other aggregation operators $A:[0,1]^{L^n}	o[0,1]$ (in case (a)) or functionals $A$ acting on measurable truth-functions on $[0,1]^n$ (in case (b)) — beyond the weighted arithmetic mean and the integral — are suitable as definitions of meta-degrees in quantitative logic. Characterize the structural properties (e.g. monotonicity, idempotence, symmetry, continuity, compatibility with logical connectives) that such an aggregation operator should satisfy, and explain how the appropriate choice of operator depends on the intended applications of the resulting quantitative logic.
